title: Recommended temperature metrics for carbon budget estimates, model evaluation and climate policy
problem: The inconsistent use of different global mean temperature metrics and reference periods creates significant variations in remaining carbon budget estimates, affecting their size and complicating the scientific assessment of Paris Agreement goals and their communication to policymakers.
method: To reconcile discrepancies in carbon budget estimates, this paper proposes an application-dependent framework for selecting global temperature metrics—recommending GSAT for scientific budgets, GBST for model evaluation, and a specific hybrid metric (PAGTM) for assessments related to the Paris Agreement.
task: The task is to recommend appropriate global mean temperature metrics for carbon budget estimates, model evaluation, and climate policy, explaining how the choice of metric influences the budget size and ensures consistency for different scientific and policy applications.
innovation: This paper explains that recent increases in remaining carbon budget estimates are due to different temperature metrics and recommends application-dependent metrics to provide consistent and transparent information for climate science and policy-making related to the Paris Agreement.
